correctness.rationale: For each selected outer vertex, the exact defensive condition is \(k_i\ge\lfloor m_i/2\rfloor+1-h\), where \(h\) is hub occupancy. With the hub present, the exact hub condition is \(\sum_i k_i\ge\lfloor N/2\rfloor\). If the hub is absent, proper petal alliances force just one petal at its threshold. If the hub is present, a petal above its center-present threshold contains a proper hub-free defensive subset. Thus \(k_i\) is zero or \(\lfloor m_i/2\rfloor\). Summing those caps and using the parity identity yields \(q\le1\), with all caps attained. The reverse direction excludes every proper subset by its hub status. All labelled choices are counted exactly and all boundary sizes (including singleton petals) are covered. An independent definition-level verifier checked 495 profiles and 1,462,825 vertex subsets; this finite check is not treated as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural family of chordal/cograph clique-windmills with unrestricted unequal petal sizes receives a complete classification of all critical defensive coalitions, despite nonmonotone alliance feasibility. The parity obstruction at the hub and friendship graphs with only sizes \(2\) and \(r+1\) yield a structural extinction theorem and unbounded gaps; the formula supplies exact multiplicities and distinguishes the global notion from the local one. These are meaningful finite-combinatorial results, not a parameter substitution or a claim of general complexity advances.
